title: Dedicated Capacity: Q3 Cadence, Initiative Phasing, and Failure-Mode Rehearsal Plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a timeboxed Q3 roadmap slice and operational playbook for Dedicated capacity that sequences autoscale experiments, prewarm/hedge windows, and failure-mode rehearsals. The goal is to reduce outage blast radius and improve SLO maintenance under surges while preserving unit economics.

Scope:
- Define a 12-week experiment cadence (three 4-week sprints) covering: predictive warm pools, tenant-level fairshare, hedged reservoir windows, and graceful-degradation policies.
- Build runbooks for two failure rehearsals: prewarm depletion and cross-region routing failover.
- Design acceptance gates and metrics to promote experiments to production (latency percentiles, cost delta, error budget burn rate).
- Coordinate with Eng for telemetry, with Design for console rollout, and with Support/Oncall for rehearsal execution.

Why this approach: Past incidents showed cascades when prewarm pools dropped below thresholds and when fallback policies routed to incompatible model variants. Instead of large one-off launches, we will adopt phased experiments with explicit roll-forward/rollback criteria and a rehearsal cadence to validate on-call playbooks.

Key deliverables:
1) Q3 Initiative Map: sequencing of experiments, owners, and milestone dates.
2) Two executable failure-mode rehearsals with checklists, runbooks, and postmortem templates.
3) Observability playbook: dashboards + SLO dashboard slices for each experiment.
4) Promotion criteria and a small A/B rollout plan for graceful-deg policies.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full pricing model changes, cross-cloud provider procurement, and long-term pooling architecture redesigns. Those items will be tracked as separate EPICs.

Estimated timeline: kick-off 2026-02-15, experiments start 2026-03-01, rehearsal window end 2026-06-30.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Experiments inadvertently increase token unit cost. Mitigation: limit experiment traffic to 5-10% tenant sample and require a cost delta guardrail before promoting.
- Risk: Oncall fatigue from rehearsals. Mitigation: schedule rehearsals in collaboration with SRE/Support and provide simulation tooling to minimize manual intervention.

Contact and owners: Jonah Mercer (PM lead, assignee), Priya Singh (Engineering lead), Marco Alvarez (SRE), Lara Kim (Design).

2026-02-14 - Design review (Lara Kim): Console changes scoped to a single dedicated 'autoscale experiments' dashboard and one promotion modal in Rollouts UI. PRD link attached.

acceptance_criteria:
1) Initiative map published with owners and milestone dates.
2) Two failure-mode rehearsals documented with runbooks, scheduled dates, and rehearsals assigned to oncall rotations.
3) Observability dashboards created with per-experiment SLO slices and synthetic checks.
4) A/B rollout plan and promotion criteria documented; experiment traffic limited to <=10% by default.
5) Post-rehearsal postmortem template and follow-up backlog created.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: narrower experiment traffic reduces blast radius but increases time-to-signal; agreed to start narrow and widen only after safety gates.
We will pilot tenant-level fairshare for two enterprise tenants (T-237, T-421) before broader rollout.
Follow-up: create ENG spike to add 'prewarm headroom' metric and a synthetic job to exercise model-variant fallback logic.
